paper.title: Algorithm 438: Product type two-point Gauss-Legendre-Simpson integration (Collected Algorithms from ACM)
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 15(6), p. 1071 (June 1972), Algorithm 438. The frame lists it as TOMS 15,6; the archive header says Communications of the ACM, Vol. 15, No. 6, June 1972, P.1071.
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/438.gz (article DOI not verified by scout; ACM page not fetched)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 438.gz (Fortran routine P2PGS and the test driver TOMS438_PRB with its reference output in the shar file 'res'; the driver's own test functions are in driver.f)
code.archive: sha256 bda38a3451fc5c7f11334fcd459802c5eb895b69b6c27c4fc9fe3527237a74e7 (downloaded by scout 2026-11-27, 8.5 KB shar; decompressed text 359 lines, sha256 685f1bfac633e90e8e757ba1a1cbe0d1ea4df48cc183f851ed925b01525e8a61)
code.note: The archive is a shar file. Extract Makefile, driver.f, res and src.f from it, build the driver with a Fortran compiler, and run it with no input. The claim is one line of the driver's output: TEST01, the value of VINT for N = 10 (printed as 2.65082).

claim.location: Shipped reference file 'res' inside the archive (shar text lines 253-300): the block TEST01, 'Integral of F(X) * G(X) from -1 to 1, with F(X) = 1, G(X) = 1/(1+x**2)', the row 'N = 10, VINT = 2.65082'. The driver prints the same block as its output.

reference.file: 438/res (the 'res' member of the shar text; decompressed text saved by scout at scratch a/58/x/438.txt)

claim.paper_value: 2.65082 (VINT for N = 10, TEST01 of the shipped driver). Note for the rerun: the driver's header says G(X) = 1/(1+x**2) on [-1,1], whose integral is pi/2, yet it prints 'Exact: 2.65164'; the rerun must read fn00 and gn00 in driver.f to see what is actually integrated, and must not change the claim to fit.
claim.metric: VINT returned by P2PGS for N = 10 on TEST01, compared as a number
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed integrand functions in the driver; no random input)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 6 significant figures, so its rounding step is 1e-5. A rerun on IEEE arithmetic that rounds the other way differs by one unit. 2e-5 allows two units and nothing larger; the quadrature itself is deterministic at this order. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: a few quadrature evaluations.
cost.data_size: None: the driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. The archive licence is not stated; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors' driver prints quadrature values by N for a fixed integrand, and the N = 10 value needs the product-type rule to run, so it tests the code rather than a closed form (the printed 'Exact' value is not the rule's output).
